name: Organic waste valorisation (composting / biogas)
value_text: Competence is expressly assigned to the municipality by law.
justification: Law 18.695, Art. 3 d) establishes waste collection and beautification as an exclusive municipal function, constituting the express legal basis for managing organic waste in the territory. Alignment with national policy is partial: ENRO 2040 sets the target of 66% organic waste valorisation and the action is directly oriented towards that objective, but the exact fit of the municipal PACCC within the LMCC requires verification of the current consolidated text at BCN.

value_text: Capacity is limited and requires external support or strengthening.
justification: The municipality has direct operational competence over the collection and disposal of organic waste (Law 18.695 Arts. 3d and 4°), and an MMA methodological guide for municipal waste plans facilitates implementation. name: Optimisation of waste collection routes and operations
value_text: Competence is expressly assigned to the municipality by law.
justification: Law 18.695 Art. 3 d) establishes waste and beautification as an essential municipal function, and Art. 6 expressly authorises municipalities to contract private parties through public tender. The relevant condition is that the real effectiveness of the action depends on the design of the tender specifications: if these do not explicitly require route optimisation and the use of tracking technology, the municipality cannot impose it on the operator once the contract has been awarded. Management competence is mediated by the contract with the private operator — it is not fully direct.

name: Differentiated collection and source separation
value_text: Competence exists but is conditional, ambiguous, or mediated by an enabling instrument.
justification:
Law 18.695 Art. 3 d) establishes a clear municipal mandate over household collection. REP Law 20.920 and its packaging decree (DS 12/2020) define that recyclable streams are the responsibility of Management Systems, and that municipalities must coordinate with them for selective collection in their territories. Exempt Resolution No. 9/2022 of the MMA approved a municipal ordinance model enabling municipalities to incorporate the obligation to separate waste at source — but within the parameters defined by the REP decrees, not unilaterally.

The main barrier is the difficulty of imposing and enforcing source separation without national sanctioning authorisation: a municipal ordinance can establish the obligation, but lacks an effective coercive mechanism if residents do not comply, as there is no national legal obligation for households that would back a municipal sanction. No court judgement or Comptroller ruling to date expressly validates or invalidates a municipal ordinance imposing source separation beyond the parameters of DS 12/2020.

name: Landfill improvement and biogas capture
value_text: Competence belongs to another level of government; municipality cannot act independently.
justification: Landfills are final disposal facilities regulated exclusively at the national and regional level: authorisation and oversight belong to the Sanitary Authority (SEREMI of Health) under D.S. No. 189/2005 of the Ministry of Health. SEREMI of Health exercises this authority pursuant to the Sanitary Code and D.S. No. 136/2004 (MINSAL Organisational Regulations, Arts. 32° and 35°). The municipality has no competence to authorise, build, or operate landfills. Its possible role is coordination with the SEREMI of Health and the GORE to identify suitable sites and promote regional projects, but without its own decision-making power.

name: Volume-based waste fee (PAYT)
value_text: Competence exists but is conditional, ambiguous, or mediated by an enabling instrument.
justification:
DL No. 3.063 of 1979 (Municipal Revenue), Arts. 6°-9°, authorises the municipality to charge a household waste fee and regulate it through a local ordinance. Art. 7° establishes that the fee is annual and set based on the actual cost of the service. Art. 8° defines usual and ordinary collection as that which does not exceed 60 litres per day, setting that parameter as the reference for standard collection — not as a system of individualised per-household measurement. Art. 6° para. 2° expressly authorises differentiating the fee for environmental programmes that include recycling. Law 18.695 Art. 3 d) complements this authorisation as the general basis for the waste function.

Volume-based pricing in the style of modern PAYT — with individualised measurement — is not expressly defined in the legal text. It is an interpretive legal construction. The Comptroller General's administrative case law is consistent in applying the principle of strict legality to the configuration of the waste fee: Rulings No. 29.860/2006, No. 9.294/2003, and No. 30.585/2004 reiterate that municipalities lack the authority to alter the structure of the waste fee beyond what is expressly authorised by DL 3.063. Rulings No. 33.416/2016 and No. 4.059/2016 confirm that charges must adhere to the parameters of Arts. 7° and 9° of the decree. A PAYT design that departs significantly from the logic of an annual fee for usual collection will be subject to scrutiny and requires a particularly rigorous justification in the enabling ordinance. No specific Comptroller ruling to date validates or declares an individualised PAYT illegal, so the risk of challenge is prudential, not confirmed by a firm ruling. Consolidated text of DL 3.063 pending verification at BCN.
references: ["DL 3.063 Rentas Municipales — BCN", "Ley 18.695 (LOCM) — BCN", "Dictamen CGR N°29.860/2006 — vLex", "Dictamen CGR N°33.416/2016 — Contraloría", "Dictamen CGR N°4.059/2016 — vLex"]

name: Prohibition / restriction of single-use plastics
value_text: Competence exists but is conditional, ambiguous, or mediated by an enabling instrument.
justification:
Law 21.100, Arts. 1 and 3, prohibits retail establishments from providing plastic bags and sets fines for violations. Enforcement of this law in the municipal territory falls to municipalities according to the BCN implementation report: this is a power to enforce a national law, not a regulatory power in its own right.

The Second Environmental Tribunal, in its judgement of 22 December 2025 (Case R-521-2025, Papier-Mettler Chile SpA v. Ministry of the Environment), confirmed that the MMA has no power of authentic interpretation of Law 21.100 — the prohibition is strictly legal and national in character. This implies that no subnational authority, including municipalities, may alter the core of the prohibition established by the law through its own instruments. Municipalities may enforce and communicationally reinforce Law 21.100 in their territory, but cannot create new prohibitions on additional materials by ordinance without express legal authorisation. Studies on competition law and economic public order warn that additional restrictions imposed by subnational authorities could be subject to controversy due to potential anti-competitive effects.
references: ["Ley 21.100 — Bolsas plásticas — BCN", "Ley 18.695 (LOCM) — BCN", "Sentencia R-521-2025 — Segundo Tribunal Ambiental", "Expediente R-521-2025 — Tribunal Ambiental"]

value_text: Competence exists but is conditional, ambiguous, or mediated by an enabling instrument.
justification: Law 18.695 authorises the municipality to enter into agreements for waste management and to grant subsidies to non-profit legal entities that collaborate with its functions (Art. 5° g). name: Construction and demolition waste management (CDW)
value_text: Competence exists but is conditional, ambiguous, or mediated by an enabling instrument.
justification: Law 18.695 Art. 3 d) authorises the municipality to require CDW management conditions via DOM permits (LGUC / OGUC, D.S. 47/1992 MINVU). D.S. No. 4/2009 MINVU specifically regulates CDW handling and is the applicable technical standard. The relevant restriction is that the hazardous fraction of CDW — soils contaminated by List II constituents of D.S. 148/2003 MINSAL — is subject to the Sanitary Authority (SEREMI of Health), not the DOM. The municipality must verify whether CDW contains these constituents before managing it. Additionally, D.S. 4/2009 is outdated (2009), which may facilitate its challenge if the municipality requires advanced recycling conditions not expressly contemplated by the standard.

value_text: Capacity is limited and requires external support or strengthening.

name: Development of eco-parks / waste valorisation centres
value_text: Competence exists but is conditional, ambiguous, or mediated by an enabling instrument.
justification: Law 18.695 authorises the municipality to develop infrastructure on its own land (Arts. 3d and 5°). The competence exists but is conditional on a chain of enabling requirements the municipality does not control unilaterally: a relevant-scale eco-park requires entry into the SEIA (a one-to-two year process), authorisation from SEREMI MMA, and DOM permits. No legal definition of 'eco-park' exists in Chilean regulations, which creates the risk of diverse interpretations by sectoral authorities. Alignment with national policy is referential: MINVU has urban park policies and the MMA has valorisation centre guidelines, but neither constitutes a direct mandate to the municipality.

name: Biogas capture and use in wastewater treatment plants
value_text: Competence belongs to another level of government; municipality cannot act independently.
justification: Urban wastewater treatment plants are the competence of SISS (Superintendency of Sanitary Services, Law 18.902), not the municipality. The municipality may operate APR (Rural Drinking Water) in rural areas, but APR applies to drinking water, not wastewater — a fundamental distinction. Treatment plant sludge may constitute Category I hazardous waste (List I, D.S. 148/2003 MINSAL), subject to the Sanitary Authority. Biogas management adds additional regulatory complexity (emission standards, possible SEIA). No standard expressly authorises municipalities to capture biogas from wastewater, even in the rural context with their own APR.

references: ["Ley 18.902 — SISS — BCN", "D.S. 148/2003 MINSAL — Residuos peligrosos — BCN", "Ley 20.936 — ERNC — BCN", "D.S. 136/2004 Reglamento Orgánico MINSAL — BCN"]
